the IpTxA binding site on RyR1 is located between the clamp and the handle domains of the channel.
imperatoxin A binds to RyR1 between clamp and handle domains.

the three-dimensional structure of the ryanodine receptor (RyR) from skeletal muscle (the RyR1 isoform), a major intracellular calcium release channel, has been determined to 23 Å resolution, and the location of a specific peptide toxin, imperatoxin a (IpTxa), on the structure has been identified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the calcium release channels/ryanodine receptors and the mechanism of their regulation.
the structural and functional properties of calcium channels, and their regulation by endogenous and exogenous ligands.
the structural and functional properties of calcium release channels (ryanodine receptors) and calcium entry channels (dihydropyridinereceptors).

the IpTxA binds to the cytosolic moiety of RyRs between the clamp and the handle domains, 12 nm away from the pore.
the IpTxA binding site on the RyR1 is at a position between the clamp and the handle domain, and that this site is a potential excition-contraction signal site.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that cryo-electron microscopy, combined with single-particle three-dimensional image analysis, can provide the three-dimensional structural information needed to understand the molecular mechanism of action of a protein complex.

the binding site for the IpTxa toxin on the RyR1 channel is located between the clamp and the handle domains, approximately 11 nm away, from the transmembranous pore, in an area of the RyR1 that has been implicated as a potential excitation contraction signal transduction site by the DHPR II-III loop.
IpTxa is the first toxin to be localized in the three-dimensional structure of a calcium channel and that it binds at an intracellular site that may play a role in excitation-contractions coupling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IpTxA binding location is a novel potential excitation- contraction coupling signal transduction site on the calcium release channel.
the three-dimensional structure of a protein can be used to predict the location of its ligand binding site.
the IpTxA binding site on RyR1 is located between two domains of the protein, the clamp domain and the handle domain.
